Accessibility

Last updated 21 October 2026

I want this site to be usable by as many people as possible. I'm aiming for WCAG 2.2 level AA. This statement is a work in progress, and I haven't had the site formally audited.

What I've done

  • Text is black on light pastel backgrounds, which gives strong contrast.
  • If your device is set to reduce motion, the zooming animation and spinning logo are switched off and the sections follow each other as an ordinary page.
  • Everything can be reached with a keyboard. Tabbing to a link scrolls it into view.
  • Pages use headings and landmarks, and the text is real text (no text in images).
  • Fonts are hosted on the site and text resizes with your browser settings.

Known limitations

  • The home page is built around a scroll-driven animation. The scrolling is animated by the site, so it can feel different from a normal page, and the animation can't be paused other than with the reduce-motion setting above.
  • The opening loader animation plays once per browser tab.
  • Some text is small. Zooming the page in will make it larger.
  • I haven't yet tested with a range of screen readers, so there may be issues I don't know about.

Tell me if something doesn't work

If you hit a barrier, or you'd like content in another format, email zcbarakat@gmail.com. I'll aim to reply within a few working days and to fix what I can.

If you're not happy with my response, you can contact the Equality Advisory and Support Service at equalityadvisoryservice.com.
